title: fix(plugin-detail,fields): the highlight strip ellipsizes a cut value, sizes a format-declared phone as a phone, starts every wrapped line flush, and is one layout below sm (objectui#12523)
body:
Fixes #12523
Clause-②: no (layout classes in the strip and three link cells; no type, prop or export changes)

## What the landing seat's browser reading should show

On the HotCRM lead "Mira Costa" record page:

- **At 1440:** Phone reads "+1-555-0117-1119" whole. It now starts a second line of the strip, flush left like the first line, with no rule and no indent. Email reads "mira.costa@atlasconstruction.example.com" whole on the first line. If a value is too long for its line, it ends in an ellipsis and its tooltip carries the whole value.
- **At 390:** the six chips share one layout. Each chip is one full-width line (label above value), with no separator rule and no indent. All six values read whole.

## What was measured before the change

Measured on `c3de0bc73d` in Chromium 1194 with the Inter font. The harness renders the real `HeaderHighlight` markup (React server render) with the console's compiled Tailwind sheet, using the lead's own field shapes:

- At a 1088px row (1440 viewport), all six chips sat on one line at 144 / 144 / 144 / 256 / 256 / 144 px. The floors added up to exactly the row, so `grow` had nothing to hand out.
- **Phone was on the 9rem floor.** HotCRM declares it `Field.text({ format: 'phone' })`. `resolveCellRendererType` reads the format and draws the phone cell. The wide-basis rule read the declared `text` and gave the chip 9rem. That is the cut objectui#11659 gave phones the 16rem basis to prevent.
- **No chip ever went past its line.** Each chip's right edge was at or inside the row's, and the Phone chip ended exactly at it. The cut was made by the value's own `truncate` span: Email had a scroll width of 322 in a 215 box, Phone 167 in 103.
- **That span could not draw an ellipsis.** Its only child was the link cell's `inline-flex` box. CSS Overflow 3 clips the first atomic inline on a line and never ellipses it. So the value was cut mid-word.
- At a 358px row (390 viewport): line 1 held Status and Lead Score. Lead Source, Lead Owner, Email and Phone then each sat alone on a line, each keeping its left rule and 20px indent. That is the "grid, then an indented list" in the card's screenshot.

## What changed

1. **`@object-ui/fields`: the email, URL and phone cells fit a bounded single-line slot with an ellipsis.**
   - These cells now follow the convention `TruncatedText` states for that file.
   - Email: the cell's box gets `max-w-full`. The anchor becomes a `block min-w-0 truncate` box: it was `Button`'s `inline-flex`, which put the text in an anonymous flex item that no `text-overflow` reaches. The copy button gets `shrink-0`.
   - URL: the anchor is the cell's root, so it becomes `inline-block max-w-full truncate align-top`.
   - Phone: the box gets `max-w-full` and the anchor `min-w-0`. The number gets its own `truncate` span, and the icon and copy button get `shrink-0`.
   - A host wider than the value sees no change.
2. **`HeaderHighlight`: a chip is sized by the cell it draws.** The wide-basis rule's display half now reads the same `drawnType` that picks the renderer, so a `text` + `format: phone` (or `email` / `url`) chip gets the 16rem floor. The relational half still reads the declared type, because the declared type is what picks the editor. With the right floors, the measured lead's floors add up to more than the row, so Phone wraps before anything is cut. The ruling describes exactly this.
3. **`HeaderHighlight`: a wrapped line starts flush.** Every chip now carries the separator and its padding. From `sm` up, the row is pulled left by one chip's separator plus its left padding. A left-edge-only `clip-path` then hides exactly what lands outside the strip, which is every line-start rule. The clip leaves 1.5 spacing units visible so an editable value's hover background (`-mx-1.5`) still shows. The other three sides are not clipped.
4. **`HeaderHighlight`: one layout below `sm`.** Every chip gets `max-sm:basis-full max-sm:max-w-full max-sm:border-l-0 max-sm:px-0`. The classes are the same for a wide chip, a narrow chip or an editing chip.

## After the change, same harness, at the final head

- **1088px row:** line 1 is Status, Lead Score, Lead Source, Lead Owner and Email (Email grows to 350px, whole). Line 2 is Phone (256px, whole), flush left. No box in any chip clips.
- **800px row (1024 viewport):** line 1 has four chips. Line 2 is Email and Phone, both whole, with Email flush left.
- **358px row:** six full-width lines, no rule, no indent, every value whole.
- **Long values** (a 68-character email, a URL and a phone with an extension, at 1088 and at 358): each ends in an ellipsis drawn by the cell's own text box. No box is clipping without one.
- **The objectui#11684 product strip** (the "QA Widget 1" SKU) at 1088 is unchanged: three chips at 144px on one line, every value whole.

## The three-section answers

- **A1: falsified.** `max-w-max` never let a chip outgrow its line: the floors decide the lines, and `grow` hands out only what is left. The cut came from the 9rem phone floor plus an inline-flex cell that cannot be ellipsed.
- **Ruling 1 deviation, said openly:** `max-w-max` is KEPT. The ruling's parenthetical ("its max-w is its share of the row, not max-content") rests on A1's mechanism. Swapping in `max-w-full` would change nothing at the measured row, which has no free width. On a row with free width it would let a chip that already fits keep taking width away from the chips that still need it, which is objectui#11684's distribution reversed. The ruling's intent is met by items 1 and 2 above:
  - a value is cut only by its own box, with an ellipsis and its whole value as `title`;
  - no chip is cut by the row;
  - when the floors exceed the row, the strip wraps before it cuts.

  Because of this, the objectui#11684 pin file is byte-identical and green. The suggested ablation ("put `max-w-max` back") does not apply, since it was never removed. The ablations actually run are listed below.
- **A2: class and structure pins, no stubbed widths.** happy-dom loads no stylesheet and has no layout, so a stubbed `scrollWidth` would only measure the stub. The objectui#11684 pins are class-semantics pins as well; they stub no widths. The pixel half is the Chromium harness above plus the landing seat's browser reading.
- **A3: full-width lines.** In two columns of a 358px row, a value gets at most about 179px, and the second column also loses its separator and padding. The measured phone cell is 167px wide and the email 322px. So the email is cut in either column and the phone in the second, and a touch screen cannot hover a `title`. Full-width lines show both whole. The cost: the strip is one line taller at 390, six lines instead of five, about 56px.
- **A4: all three callers covered.** `HeaderHighlight` is called by `DetailView`, by the `record:highlights` renderer (the record page, authored pages and the drawer) and by `RecordPreviewCard`. The drawer's objectui#11684 pins are unchanged and green, and so are the preview card's tests.

## File surface

- **Within the claim:** `HeaderHighlight.tsx`, its new pin file, and one changeset.
- **Outside the predicted surface, under the producer clause of the dispatch:** `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` (the three link cells) and its pin file. The measurement put the missing ellipsis in the cells, not the chip. The changeset therefore names `@object-ui/fields` (patch) beside `@object-ui/plugin-detail` (patch).
- Not touched: `DetailView.tsx`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`, and every export, prop and type.

## Tests and gates

All runs below are at head `28283919de`, the final commit. Every test run is from the repository root and went through the objectstack verify lock.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/ packages/fields/` (full suites of both packages): 528 files passed, 2 skipped; 6707 tests passed, 21 skipped; exit 0.
- New pins: `HeaderHighlight.lineFitAndPhoneLayout-12523.test.tsx` (9 tests) and `cellRenderers.linkEllipsis-12523.test.tsx` (5 tests), both green.
- Existing highlight pins, green with no edits:
  - `HeaderHighlight.shareRowWidth-11684` (the objectui#11684 pins)
  - `RecordHighlightsRenderer.phoneWidth-11659`
  - `RecordHighlightsRenderer.percentClip`
  - `expandableFamily.identity-5874`
- Consumers, 15 files, 100 tests, exit 0:
  - the strip: the seven `RecordDetailView.*` tests that render highlights, `RecordPreviewCard`, and `record-pointer-card-renderer`;
  - the link cells: `ObjectGrid.linkCellNoNestedAnchor-11817`, `formatHintedColumnRenderer-8920`, `ObjectDataTable.cells`, `recordFields.formatHintNotDatePattern-10220`, `ObjectGallery.cells` and `ReportViewer.cells`.
- Census tests whose subject this diff touches all ran inside the full package suites:
  - in `fields`: `cellRenderers.fabricatedValue-8490`, `cellRenderers.objectLiteral-8596`, `cellRenderers.valueIndependent-8678`, `cellRenderers.childlessContainer-8580` and `RecordPickerDialog.layout-11903`;
  - in `plugin-detail`: `summaryChip.badgeFitCensus-8464`.
- Type check. The closure build `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build` (exit 0) ran first, because `type-check` depends on `^build`. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` both exited 0. Each echoed its script, and each includes the package's tests through `tsconfig.test.json`. Known red, not chased here: objectui#12422's build-order race may red CI `Type Check` when `plugin-detail#build` re-runs.
- Run locally, each with its exit code read before any pipe:
  - eslint on the four changed source and test files (exit 0, 0 errors);
  - `check:control-bytes` (exit 0) and `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations, exit 0);
  - `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite` and `check-changeset-claims` (all exit 0);
  - `check-vi-mock-override-shape` and `check-test-path-roots` (both exit 0).
- Left to CI: the repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`), the sharded `pnpm test`, and Build & E2E.

## Ablation

Every leg ran with `ablation-replace` (the anchor must hit, the write is checked on disk, and the restore is proved: the blob equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is empty). The pins import the source through the vitest alias, so no `dist` is involved.

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The wide rule reads `resolvedType` again | Both format-floor pins red, 7 green |
| 2 | The below-`sm` class line deleted | Both one-layout pins red |
| 3 | `first:border-l-0 first:pl-0` put back | The every-chip-separator pin red |
| 4a | The email anchor's classes reverted | The email pin red |
| 4b | The phone number's `truncate` span removed | The phone pin red |
| 4c | The URL anchor's classes reverted | The URL pin red |

Leg 4b's first attempt did not run. The tool refused it before running anything, because the replacement text `{safe}` occurs elsewhere and its count could not prove the write. It was re-run with a two-line anchor, and the table records that run.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- Other cells whose root is a multi-element inline box (the location / geolocation cell, the color swatch) can still be cut without an ellipsis in a squeezed chip. This is the residue objectui#4054 described; that card ended as not planned. No user-visible instance was reproduced here. No carrier.
- `isKpi` still reads the declared type, so a `text` field with `format: currency` or `format: percent` does not get `tabular-nums`. This is cosmetic, and no carrier.
- The strip at 390 is about 56px taller, as stated under A3.
